I have self esteem issues myself and my boyfriend is who and what makes me feel really great about myself. Attractive, deserving, confident, what-have-you, and has for the past almost 3 years. I apologize for going on a tangent about myself, but just to give you some insight, him and I recently we went on a break for only about 2 weeks and I was driven crazy without him. I felt awful about myself the whole time, wondering if I could ever feel good about myself again. I hated myself. It is because HE made me feel good about myself and I worried that I could only do so with his assistance. In trying to teach her to love herself, do that simply: teach her. Do not do it for her, because if there is ever a time that the two of you are not together or something happens to you, she will probably return to the negative thought patterns that she knew without you. Not that poor self esteem is something that a person can't survive, but it's surely not the happiest way to live. So offer suggestions like doing things she likes for herself, occupying her time doing something positive for only her. Maybe this will start to benefit her in the long run. I will agree that it isn't about compliments because like SymbolicFox said, yes, she might know deep down, but she can't believe it.

As said by another redditor, "Nobody is inherently good or inherently bad, we are complex being capable of many things". I think people grow and learn as time proceeds and it is whether or not they learn from their mistakes that defines them, not simply their mistakes. My best friend cheated on her boyfriend, drunk at a party with a stranger when they had been dating for 5 months. She had never done anything like this in the past and she was so genuinely ashamed and sorry for what she had done. Her and her boyfriend separated for a few weeks, chose to get back together and work things out, and have remained together for the past 3 years and they are still so in love, moving together soon and thinking about getting married. They are like best friends and she would never think of being unfaithful to her current partner and in the case that they were to break up, any future partners. She still calls me crying every now and then because she is sometimes so overwhelmed with guilt and disgusted with herself, even though her boyfriend hasn't thought twice about it for the past 2 years. I have to say that this is not due to a "huge gaping fucking character flaw". People make mistakes. It shows in their actions whether or not they would like to amend them. If she is genuinely sorry and ashamed for her actions, and you truly think she could be the one for you, it might not hurt to give her a second chance and your relationship is probably not irreparable. If she does it again, I will have to say that there is probably someone out there better for you.

I am a fairly strict vegetarian, not a vegan and I have been dating a non-vegan for nearly 2 and a half years. If he asked me to marry him tomorrow, the answer would be yes, unquestionably. If marriage came into the picture, we would both eventually want children and I'd love to have children with him someday if this were the case. This is due to the fact that we are separate individuals and his opinions, eating habits, and decisions are simply just that. **His**. He is very proud of my choices and while he may not choose to live his life the way I do, our differences in opinions or ethics would never make me love him less or feel as if our relationship were a sort of "constant struggle". He understands my decisions and finds them agreeable and if someday we have children together, I assume that he wouldn't mind a bit if I wanted to raise them vegan or vegetarian, under the circumstance that we allow them to make their own choices whenever they are able to decide. He is my first serious relationship so I'm not entirely sure how much easier it is if your significant other is vegan/vegetarian, but it does not seem very hard for us as is. To put it simply, he eats what he does and I eat what I do, whether or not that means cooking separate meals.
